ideas.title: Seeds that spin down and plant a forest
ideas.critique: It reuses the falling-plate model from the last two posts, so the payoff of a thing spinning down through simulated air is already familiar. What's new is autorotation, thousands of seeds batched on the GPU and landings that really change where the flora grows, but only if the spin comes out of the physics and isn't a rotation added on top.

ideas.title: A tiny planet over the meadow
ideas.critique: A local gravity field with things in orbit is the island's ring rule again at a smaller scale, and it is the same 'new world rule acted out' form that has just failed twice. A friend walking upside down is a picture people would share, but feet that follow a gravity vector are hard, and the likely version is a reoriented walk on a sphere.

ideas.title: The camera obscura
ideas.critique: This is real light transport that no raster trick fakes, and it suits the RayMakie showcase exactly. But a pinhole image is extremely dim and noisy in a path tracer, so few samples will give you mush, and once you have seen it there is not much to come back for.

ideas.title: After the rain, everything is wet
ideas.critique: Wet surfaces after rain are a stock feature of polished games and the first thing anyone would expect from the rendering goal, and it is the third look-change in a row. A wetness field that dries from the edges and keeps footprints is more than a material swap, but watching it is mostly a slow fade.

ideas.title: Footsteps you can hear
ideas.critique: Sound is a channel the island has never used, and modal synthesis from material, size and the mass of the foot is a real system that later things can build on. The risk is that it ends up as a lookup table of samples, or that browser audio never ships, which would leave a silent film.

ideas.title: Lumi pulls a rickshaw
ideas.critique: A jointed cart the player can pull, with load and a slope that really push back, is good to play. But the runaway that tips the passenger into the flowers reads like a planned gag, and PrintSim contact already broke on a sheet of paper, so a cart on the terrain is a big risk.

ideas.title: A torn letter
ideas.critique: Added mass and the Munk moment, so that size alone decides between gliding and tumbling, is a real physics step for the paper project. To a viewer, though, it is a third post in a row of paper falling in slow motion, and the novelty has worn off.

ideas.title: Bored Lumi kicks a pebble
ideas.critique: This is the ball that rolls downhill and gets kicked between friends, which the island tried twice recently and never landed. Tying the kick to the mood file is honest, but the payoff is the same.

ideas.title: Shadow theatre at night
ideas.critique: Shadows from a point light that soften and grow with distance are real in the tracer and give the night a strong picture. The posing is a scripted reaction, though, and shadow gags have been on the island twice just now.

ideas.title: The ice breaks into floes
ideas.critique: Buoyancy from submerged volume and floes that tilt under a walker give the frozen sea something it lacked: things you can play with that answer your weight. It is still breaking something the island has, though, and IPC contact among many floes is the same contact that broke the letter.
